classification.difficultyReason: Part c requires recognising that the two isosceles triangles determine the sum of two individually unknown angles, introducing separate angle variables and combining them through the quadrilateral sum without finding either separately.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals, giving reasons.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle PQR with C on PQ, D on QR and segment CD.
spec.mathematics: QP=QR; angle PCD=158 degrees; angle CDR=68 degrees; angle QPR=beta.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}\angle QCD&=180^\circ-158^\circ\\\angle QCD&=22^\circ\\\angle CDQ&=180^\circ-68^\circ\\\angle CDQ&=112^\circ\\\angle C Q D&=180^\circ-22^\circ-112^\circ\\\angle C Q D&=46^\circ\\\beta&=(180^\circ-46^\circ)\div2\\\beta&=67^\circ\end{align*}$

Straight angles at $C$ and $D$; angle sum of triangle $QCD$; equal base angles of isosceles triangle $PQR$.

spec.description: Pentagon ABCDE with equal-side marks, dashed auxiliary segments BM, BD and DN, and a perpendicular from C to AE.
spec.mathematics: BC=CD; AB=BM=DN=DE; C's full angle is 108 degrees; angle AND=108 degrees; BD and AE are perpendicular to the same vertical segment. Alpha is angle BDN.

answer.worked:
$BD\parallel AE$, since both are perpendicular to the same line.

$\begin{align*}\alpha+108^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=72^\circ\end{align*}$

Co-interior angles on parallel lines $BD$ and $AE$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral PQRS with QS drawn, matching ticks on PS, QS and RS, and a right angle PSR. The alpha arc spans the full angle PQR across QS.
spec.mathematics: PS=QS=RS and PS perpendicular to SR.

answer.short:
$\alpha=135^\circ$

Add the base angles of the two isosceles triangles.
answer.worked:
Let $\angle PQS=x$ and $\angle SQR=y$.

$\angle QPS=x$ because $PS=QS$, and $\angle QRS=y$ because $QS=RS$.

$\begin{align*}2x+2y+90^\circ&=360^\circ\\2(x+y)&=270^\circ\\x+y&=135^\circ\\\alpha&=135^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of quadrilateral $PQRS$ and equal base angles of isosceles triangles.

spec.description: Quadrilateral PQRS with four labelled interior angles.
spec.answerVisibility: No numerical value for alpha is shown.

spec.description: Triangles ABD and BDC share dashed BD; ADC is a right angle and AD, DB and DC have matching single ticks.
spec.mathematics: AD=DB=DC; angle ADC=90 degrees; angle DBC=28 degrees; alpha is angle DAB.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown alpha are displayed.

answer.worked:
$DB=DC$, so $\angle BCD=\angle DBC=28^\circ$ (equal base angles of isosceles triangle $BDC$).

$\begin{align*}\angle BDC&=180^\circ-28^\circ-28^\circ\\\angle BDC&=124^\circ\\\angle ADB&=360^\circ-90^\circ-124^\circ\\\angle ADB&=146^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of triangle $BDC$; angles in a revolution at $D$.

$AD=DB$, so the base angles of triangle $ADB$ are equal.

$\begin{align*}\alpha&=(180^\circ-146^\circ)\div2\\\alpha&=17^\circ\end{align*}$

spec.description: Quadrilateral DABC with E on DC and EB drawn.
spec.mathematics: ADE=42 degrees; ABE=22 degrees; BEC=22 degrees; EBC=BCE=alpha; DAB=beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angles and alpha/beta labels are shown.

answer.worked:
$\begin{align*}2\alpha+22^\circ&=180^\circ\\2\alpha&=158^\circ\\\alpha&=79^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of triangle $EBC$.

$\begin{align*}\beta+42^\circ+22^\circ+79^\circ+79^\circ&=360^\circ\\\beta+222^\circ&=360^\circ\\\beta&=138^\circ\end{align*}$

Angle sum of quadrilateral $DABC$.
